Adding the architect's clarifications (will be included in a 1-paragraph appendix):

- Dedicated: tenant receives reserved GPU pool nodes behind a dedicated subnet. Control plane is nevertheless routed through a separate management VPC with strict RBAC. Hardware isolation: yes (reserved tenancy on GPU nodes, no noisy neighbor at the node level).

- Private (VPC): customer traffic terminates at customer VPC peering or PrivateLink. Tenant workloads run in containers on shared GPU nodes with tenant fencing via kernel namespaces + runtime policies. KV cache is per-tenant logically separated; we persist only encrypted blobs with tenant-specific keys.

Mini diagram (ASCII, for clarity — full PNG will be attached):

  [Customer VPC] ---peer---> [Redwood Private Edge] ---mtu--> [Inference Cluster (shared nodes)]
                                  |
                                  +--> [Control Plane (multitenant, IAM)]

Egress controls:
- Egress is forced through an application gateway with allowlist + NAT per-customer (redwood-managed) for Private customers; dedicated customers may attach customer-managed NAT.
- All egress is logged to central SIEM with tenant tags.

I'll finalize the appendix and hand over the PNG/PDF shortly.

Ben Carter
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
